criteria.note: CONSUME a W8 crossing and DRAFT a restoration intent naming the area, the crossed rule, and the expected post-restoration measure. restoration.py loads .warp/entropy.py the way entropy loads metrics/validate (importlib.util spec_from_file_location), calls entropy.entropy_report over the injected events, and filters report['crossings'] through trusted_crossings (not c.get('advisory')) - it adds NO second detection, NO second aggregation, and NO second parser (the front-matter parser is validate.parse_yamlish reached through entropy.V). render_draft names area (crossing.area), crossed_rule (crossing.dimension), and expected_post_restoration_measure {dimension, target == baseline, condition <= baseline}, and records a before block {latest, baseline, relative_increase}. I reproduced independently over a seeded TRUSTED crossing (core/human_minutes, latest 30 vs baseline 10, advisory False): draft_from_crossings created exactly one file core__human_minutes.yaml; the loaded draft carries area == core, crossed_rule == human_minutes, expected_post_restoration_measure.dimension == human_minutes with target 10.0, and before.latest 30.0 / before.baseline 10.0. Non-vacuity confirmed by mutation MUT4 (dropping the before block from render_draft leaves the loaded draft with no before key, which the AC1 before-measure test catches).

The draft is a DRAFT only a HUMAN promotes (NG2); the machine authors no spec and self-promotes nothing. render_draft emits schema warp.restoration/v1, status draft, drafted_by 'warp-entropy-pass (machine draft; a human promotes it into a warp.spec/v1 restoration spec)', drafted_at, and carries NONE of decider/chosen/decided_by/promoted/promoted_by. It is homed per-repo under .warp/restorations/<area>__<dimension>.yaml, a directory NO gate module sweeps: I grep'd .warp/*.py, scripts/*.py and scripts/*.sh and only restoration.py itself (and the selftest) reference .warp/restorations/; validate.py sweeps .warp/decisions, .warp/readings, .warp/redecisions but never .warp/restorations, so a draft is inert per-repo data that never reaches the frontier. I reproduced over a temp tree with a specs/ dir: after drafting, the draft carries status draft and none of decider/chosen/promoted, drafting wrote only core__human_minutes.yaml under .warp/restorations/, and specs/ stayed EMPTY (the machine authored no spec). The human-promote boundary is architecturally correct: the machine writes the intent; a human reads it and authors the warp.spec/v1. Nothing in the module flips a restoration to active work, and nothing writes to specs/. This is the decay-class analogue of WARP-1107's draft_redecisions (which I confirmed mirrors: idempotent, human-promoted, per-repo subdir the glob does not sweep).

IDEMPOTENT, advisory does not draft, adoption safe. crossing_key returns '%s__%s' % (area, dimension); draft_from_crossings computes dst = rdir/(key + '.yaml') and, if dst.exists(), appends (key, 'exists') and continues WITHOUT rewriting - an existing draft is never overwritten. I reproduced independently: a first derivation drafts exactly one (created); a second derivation of the SAME crossing at a LATER injected date (2027-01-01) drafts none (exists) and the file is byte-identical to the first; a DIFFERENT crossing (core/tokens) drafts a distinct file core__tokens.yaml; an ADVISORY crossing (advisory True) drafts nothing and the restorations dir is not even created; and draft_restorations over a contract-free tree returns standdown True with no drafts and no restorations dir. Non-vacuity confirmed by two mutations: MUT1 (removing the advisory guard) makes an advisory crossing draft, which the AC3 advisory test catches; MUT2 (removing the dst.exists guard) re-creates and rewrites the draft on re-derive (byte-changed), which the idempotency test catches.

The post-restoration measure CLOSES THE LOOP on the cost delta, and the module is IN-SESSION only with nothing auto-gating or auto-promoting. restoration_delta reads before.latest/before.baseline from the draft and after_latest (the area's current cost-to-change for the crossed dimension, read from the SAME W8 report via _area_latest, never a recompute), returns delta = before_latest - after (positive when cost dropped) and paid_off = (after is not None and before_baseline is not None and after <= before_baseline), and reports measured False before a restoration ships. I reproduced independently: a restoration that dropped the cost (after 8) reports delta 22 and paid_off True; a cost that did not drop (after 30) reports delta 0 and paid_off False (non-vacuous); pre-ship (after None) reports measured False; and the boundary case after == baseline (10) correctly reports paid_off True (<=, not <). IN-SESSION/NO-DAEMON confirmed: restoration.py imports only argparse/importlib.util/json/sys/datetime/pathlib and contains NONE of subprocess/Popen/os.fork/os.exec/os.spawn/os.system/setsid/nohup/start_new_session/multiprocessing/threading/asyncio/sched (my own grep) and no network primitive (socket/urllib/http/requests/httpx/aiohttp). I reproduced the mutation teeth: appending a detached subprocess.Popen(claude -p, start_new_session=True), a daemon Thread, and an os.fork() each turned the no-detach scan RED, and the real module on disk was byte-unchanged after. NOTHING auto-gates / auto-promotes: by my own grep the only 'restoration' hits in gate-path files are docstring PROSE (shape_gate.py:35, validate.py:953); '.warp/restoration.py' is absent from verify.sh, shape_gate.py, and validate.py, and 'draft_restorations' is absent from validate.py, so no crossing fails the build and no draft is promoted without a human. Only selftest.py loads the module.
